name: Forest-tundra / krummholz
notes: Forest-tundra ecotone and treeline krummholz: wind-stunted conifers, dwarf birch/willow, heath and lichen mats. Drawn on Scandinavia/Siberia (birch-spruce), Rockies (spruce-fir) and Alps (mountain pine).

canopy.name: Wind-stunted conifer
canopy.source: Picea engelmannii, Rocky Mountain treeline 2700-3600 m, forms krummholz mats and flagged trees 1-8 m

canopy.name: Mountain birch
canopy.source: Betula pubescens (subsp. czerepanovii), Fennoscandian and Icelandic treeline, crooked multi-stemmed birch 2-8 m

canopy.name: Dahurian larch
canopy.source: Larix gmelinii, northern Siberia treeline on permafrost, world's northernmost tree; stunted 3-10 m at forest-tundra edge

shrub.name: Mountain pine
shrub.source: Pinus mugo, Alps/Carpathians/Balkans subalpine 1400-2700 m, prostrate multi-stem krummholz 1-3 m

shrub.name: Dwarf willow
shrub.source: Salix glauca, circumboreal treeline and tundra, grey-leaved shrub 0.3-1.5 m along streams

shrub.name: Dwarf birch
shrub.source: Betula nana, circumpolar forest-tundra and bog, 0.2-1.2 m

shrub.name: Heath
shrub.source: Vaccinium myrtillus (bilberry), Eurasian subalpine heath and birch forest floor, 20-60 cm; Empetrum/Vaccinium heath dominant at treeline

ground.name: Mountain avens
ground.source: Dryas octopetala, Arctic-alpine Eurasia/N America, evergreen mat on calcareous ground

ground.name: Star reindeer lichen
ground.source: Cladonia stellaris, circumboreal forest-tundra, pale star-shaped lichen mats dominant on dry lichen heath

ground.name: Sheep fescue
ground.source: Festuca ovina, Eurasian and N American mountain heath, fine-leaved tussock grass 10-30 cm
